verdict.rationale: Orama documents its own incremental insertion APIs (`insert`, `insertMultiple` with batching) for the JS library. Orama Cloud data sources are segregated, so you can update, delete, or add data in one source without affecting the others, which avoids a project-wide rebuild. However, the evidence never states that updates and deletes at the document level become searchable in near real time, or that no reindex of the affected data source is needed. Missing for 10: documented single-document update/remove APIs, explicit near-real-time visibility or latency guarantees, a statement that changes apply without reindexing the affected data source, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, document adds, updates, and deletes become searchable in near real time without a full reindex

citations.quote: Every data source is segregated from the others, so you can update, delete, or add new data without affecting the data in the other data sources.
insertion in Orama is quick and intuitive
If you have a lot of records, we suggest using the insertMultiple function... You can pass a third, optional, parameter to change the batch size (default: 1000).
